around.headline: Bengaluru man duped after sharing OTP and KYC details in a 'fancy mobile number' offer
around.summary: A Bengaluru man was defrauded after a caller offering him a 'fancy' (easy-to-remember) mobile number talked him into sharing an OTP and KYC documents, per The Times of India. Never share an OTP over a call, whatever the pitch — it's the one thing a scammer needs to take over your number or accounts.

around.headline: Man killed by relative in J.P. Nagar shop dispute
around.summary: A man was murdered inside a J.P. Nagar shop by a distant relative following a dispute over demand for a separate shop, per The Hindu and Deccan Herald. A reminder that property and business disputes with relatives can escalate fast — involve police or mediation early rather than letting tempers build.

around.headline: Wilson Garden police bust fake car document racket, 10 vehicles seized
around.summary: Police busted a racket using forged RCs, bank NOCs and seals to sell cars, seizing 10 vehicles, per Deccan Herald and The Hindu. Before buying a used car, verify the RC and any loan-NOC directly on the Parivahan portal rather than trusting paperwork shown by the seller.

around.headline: Metro Pink Line clears key hurdle: Railway Board approves BEML trains
around.summary: The Railway Board has approved running BEML train sets on the Pink Line's elevated section, with CMRS safety clearance next before it can open to the public — likely mid-October, per ETV Bharat and Deccan Herald. Commuters on the Pink Line corridor can expect the new stretch to open within weeks once the safety sign-off comes through.

around.headline: Karnataka drafts law to keep schoolteachers off non-teaching duties
around.summary: The state government is drafting a law to stop schoolteachers from being pulled into non-teaching government work such as election or census duty during school hours, per The Times of India. Parents can expect fewer last-minute class disruptions if the law goes through.

around.headline: 9 killed as tourist bus catches fire in Greater Noida
around.summary: Nine people died and several were injured when a tourist bus caught fire in Greater Noida, per NDTV. Before booking a long-distance private bus, check that it has working fire extinguishers and clearly marked emergency exits — don't assume it's been inspected.

street_smart.title: You get a call from someone claiming your telecom operator is offering you a rare 'fancy' mobile number — easy to remember, almost like a VIP number — for a small fee. To 'verify and activate' it, he asks you to read out the OTP that just landed on your phone and share a photo of your Aadhaar and PAN.
street_smart.based_on: The Times of India, Sept 23-24 — a Bengaluru man was duped after a caller offering him a 'fancy mobile number' convinced him to share an OTP and KYC documents. This fancy-number-offer scam mechanism hasn't been used as a street-smart topic in the last three weeks.
street_smart.situation: The caller sounds professional, already knows your current number, and creates urgency by saying the offer and the OTP both expire in a few minutes. He's still on the line, waiting for you to read out the code.

choices.text: Read out the OTP and send photos of your Aadhaar and PAN, since the caller already has your number and the offer sounds official.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. An OTP is a one-time key meant only for you — no genuine telecom 'upgrade' or number allotment ever requires you to read one out over a call. Combined with Aadhaar and PAN photos, this gives a scammer everything needed for a SIM swap or to open fraudulent accounts in your name.

choices.text: Hang up, then call your telecom operator's official customer-care number — found on your bill or their app, not any number the caller gave — to check if such an offer genuinely exists before sharing anything.
choices.feedback: Correct. Independently dialing a number you sourced yourself breaks the scammer's control of the conversation. Genuine telecom offers don't need an OTP read aloud, and your operator's own helpline can confirm in seconds whether any 'fancy number' scheme is even running.

choices.text: Stay on the call and share your name and address, but refuse to read out the OTP, thinking partial information is harmless.
choices.feedback: Risky. Staying engaged keeps you exposed to escalating pressure tactics, and details like your name and address, combined with other leaked data, are often enough to make a follow-up scam call sound even more convincing.

choices.text: Just block the number and move on without reporting it anywhere.
choices.feedback: Risky. Blocking stops that one number, but scammers rotate numbers constantly, and an unreported attempt means the pattern isn't flagged for others. Report it so the number can be blocked network-wide.

takeaways: Never read out or share an OTP with anyone over a call, message, or in person, no matter what offer or urgency is used to justify it — it's the single credential that unlocks SIM swaps and account takeovers.
Verify any unexpected 'offer' call by hanging up and dialing your operator's official number from your bill or their app — never a number the caller provides.
Report suspicious calls to the national cyber-fraud helpline (1930) or via the Sanchar Saathi/Chakshu portal so the number gets blocked for everyone, not just you.

quiz.question: What did a Bengaluru man share that led to him being duped in the 'fancy mobile number' scam reported today?
quiz.why: Scammers used the OTP to hijack his number and the KYC documents (likely Aadhaar/PAN) to impersonate him further — a common combination behind SIM-swap fraud.

quiz.question: What did the Railway Board approve for Bengaluru Metro's Pink Line elevated section, clearing a key hurdle for its opening?
options: Running of new BEML train sets, with CMRS safety clearance next
A fare increase for the whole network
Permanent closure of the elevated stretch
A direct extension to the airport
quiz.why: CMRS (Commissioner of Metro Rail Safety) is the statutory authority that must separately inspect and clear a new metro stretch before it can carry passengers, even after trains are approved.

quiz.question: How many people died when a tourist bus caught fire in Greater Noida, per today's national news?
quiz.why: Bus fires often turn fatal quickly when exits are blocked or hard to locate — checking for marked emergency exits before boarding is a simple precaution.

quiz.question: What is the minimum age set by India's Constitution for someone to become a member of the Lok Sabha?
quiz.why: The minimum age is higher for the Rajya Sabha, India's upper house, where a member must be at least 30 years old.

quiz.question: Which gas do plants primarily absorb from the air to carry out photosynthesis?
quiz.why: Plants combine absorbed carbon dioxide with water, using sunlight, to produce glucose for energy — releasing oxygen as a by-product.
